practice: Two forces of 8 N and 6 N act at a point. Find the resultant when (a) they are in the same direction, (b) they are opposite, (c) they are perpendicular. [Solution: (a) $R = 8+6 = 14\,\text{N}$, same direction. (b) $R = 8-6 = 2\,\text{N}$, along the 8 N force. (c) $R = \sqrt{64+36} = \sqrt{100} = 10\,\text{N}$, at $\tan^{-1}(6/8) = 36.9°$ from the 8 N force.]

Two equal forces of 10 N each have a resultant of 10 N. Find the angle between them. [Solution: $R = 2P\cos(\theta/2)$, so $10 = 2(10)\cos(\theta/2)$, giving $\cos(\theta/2) = 1/2$, so $\theta/2 = 60°$ and $\theta = 120°$.]

A force of 20 N acts due east and a force of 15 N acts due north. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant. [Solution: $R = \sqrt{20^2+15^2} = \sqrt{400+225} = \sqrt{625} = 25\,\text{N}$. Direction: $\alpha = \tan^{-1}(15/20) = \tan^{-1}(3/4) \approx 36.9°$ north of east.]

Three forces of 3 N, 4 N, and 5 N act along the sides of a right triangle taken in order. Find their resultant. [Solution: Since $3^2+4^2=5^2$, these forces form a closed triangle. By the triangle law, the resultant is $\vec{R} = \vec{0}$. The system is in equilibrium.]

Two vectors $\vec{A} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$ and $\vec{B} = 5\hat{i} - 2\hat{j}$ are added. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant. [Solution: $\vec{R} = \vec{A}+\vec{B} = 8\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}$. $R = \sqrt{64+4} = \sqrt{68} \approx 8.25$. $\alpha = \tan^{-1}(2/8) = \tan^{-1}(0.25) \approx 14.0°$ from the positive x-axis.]

A boat heads north at 12 km/h in a river flowing east at 5 km/h. Find the boat's actual speed and direction relative to the ground. [Solution: $\vec{v}_{actual} = 12\hat{j} + 5\hat{i}$. Speed $= \sqrt{144+25} = 13\,\text{km/h}$. Direction $= \tan^{-1}(12/5) \approx 67.4°$ east of north (or $22.6°$ north of east).]

Find the resultant of two forces $P$ and $Q$ when the angle between them is $\theta$. If $\theta$ increases from 0° to 180°, describe qualitatively how $R$ changes. [Solution: $R = \sqrt{P^2+Q^2+2PQ\cos\theta}$. As $\theta$ increases, $\cos\theta$ decreases from 1 to -1, so $R$ decreases from $P+Q$ to $|P-Q|$. The resultant is maximum when vectors are parallel and minimum when anti-parallel.]

Two forces act at a point: $\vec{F}_1 = 10\,\text{N}$ at 30° north of east, and $\vec{F}_2 = 15\,\text{N}$ at 60° north of west. Find the resultant using component method. [Solution: $F_{1x} = 10\cos30° = 8.66$, $F_{1y} = 10\sin30° = 5.00$. $F_{2x} = -15\cos60° = -7.50$, $F_{2y} = 15\sin60° = 12.99$. $R_x = 1.16$, $R_y = 17.99$. $R = \sqrt{1.35+323.64} \approx 18.0\,\text{N}$, $\alpha = \tan^{-1}(17.99/1.16) \approx 86.3°$ north of east.]

Three forces of 4 N, 5 N, and 6 N act along the three sides of a triangle taken in order. Find the magnitude and direction of their resultant. [Solution: If taken head-to-tail around a closed triangle, the resultant is $\vec{R} = \vec{0}$. The forces form a closed polygon, so the system is in equilibrium.]

A force of 30 N acts at 0°, another at 90°, and a third at 180°. Find the resultant. [Solution: $\vec{F}_1 = 30\hat{i}$, $\vec{F}_2 = 30\hat{j}$, $\vec{F}_3 = -30\hat{i}$. $\vec{R} = 30\hat{i} + 30\hat{j} - 30\hat{i} = 30\hat{j}$. The resultant is 30 N in the +y direction.]

A force of 100 N acts at 30° to the horizontal. Find its horizontal and vertical components. [Solution: $F_x = 100\cos30° = 100\cdot(0.866) = 86.6\,\text{N}$. $F_y = 100\sin30° = 100\cdot(0.5) = 50\,\text{N}$.]

A block of 10 kg rests on a smooth inclined plane at 30° to the horizontal. Find the components of weight along and perpendicular to the plane. [Solution: $W = mg = 10\cdot9.8 = 98\,\text{N}$. Along plane: $W\sin30° = 98\cdot0.5 = 49\,\text{N}$ (down the slope). Perpendicular: $W\cos30° = 98\cdot0.866 = 84.87\,\text{N}$ (into the plane).]

Resolve a vector of magnitude 20 N along two perpendicular axes such that the component along one axis is 12 N. Find the other component and the angle. [Solution: $R^2 = R_x^2 + R_y^2$, so $R_y = \sqrt{20^2-12^2} = \sqrt{400-144} = \sqrt{256} = 16\,\text{N}$. $\theta = \cos^{-1}(12/20) = 53.1°$.]

A body moves with velocity 50 m/s at 60° north of east. Find its eastward and northward components. [Solution: $v_x = 50\cos60° = 25\,\text{m/s}$ (east). $v_y = 50\sin60° = 50\cdot0.866 = 43.3\,\text{m/s}$ (north).]

If $\vec{A} = 4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$ and $\vec{B} = 5\hat{i} - 12\hat{j}$, find the resultant. [Solution: $\vec{R} = \vec{A}+\vec{B} = 9\hat{i} - 9\hat{j}$. $R = \sqrt{81+81} = \sqrt{162} = 9\sqrt{2} \approx 12.73$. $\alpha = \tan^{-1}(-9/9) = -45°$ (below x-axis).]

Show that the resultant of two perpendicular vectors of magnitudes 5 and 12 is 13, and find the angle it makes with the 12-unit vector. [Solution: $R = \sqrt{25+144} = \sqrt{169} = 13$. $\theta = \tan^{-1}(5/12) = 22.6°$ from the 12-unit vector. By the 5-12-13 right triangle, this is the famous 3-4-5 triple scaled up.]

A force has components $F_x = -6\,\text{N}$ and $F_y = 8\,\text{N}$. Find the magnitude of the force and the angle it makes with the positive x-axis. [Solution: $F = \sqrt{36+64} = 10\,\text{N}$. $\theta = \tan^{-1}(8/(-6)) = 180° - 53.1° = 126.9°$ (second quadrant).]

A vector of magnitude 10 units makes equal angles with the x and y axes. Find its components. [Solution: If $\theta_x = \theta_y = \alpha$, then since the components are along the axes, the angle between them is 90°. The vector is along the angle bisector, so $\alpha = 45°$. Components: $R_x = R_y = 10\cos45° = 10/\sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2} \approx 7.07$.]

A force of 50 N is resolved into two components along directions making angles of 30° and 45° with the force. Find the magnitudes of the components. [Solution: Using the sine rule in the resolution triangle: $\frac{50}{\sin(180°-30°-45°)} = \frac{F_1}{\sin45°} = \frac{F_2}{\sin30°}$. The angle between the components is $180°-30°-45° = 105°$. $F_1 = 50\sin45°/\sin105° = 50(0.7071)/0.9659 = 36.6\,\text{N}$. $F_2 = 50\sin30°/\sin105° = 50(0.5)/0.9659 = 25.9\,\text{N}$.]

A particle is acted upon by three forces: 10 N along +x, 15 N at 60° from +x, and 20 N at 150° from +x. Find the resultant by resolution. [Solution: $F_{1x}=10$, $F_{1y}=0$. $F_{2x}=15\cos60°=7.5$, $F_{2y}=15\sin60°=12.99$. $F_{3x}=20\cos150°=-17.32$, $F_{3y}=20\sin150°=10$. $R_x=10+7.5-17.32=0.18$, $R_y=0+12.99+10=22.99$. $R=\sqrt{0.03+528.54}=\sqrt{528.57}\approx23.0\,\text{N}$. $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(22.99/0.18)\approx89.6°$ from +x.]

A force of 20 N acts at 60° above the horizontal. Find its horizontal and vertical components. [Solution: $F_x = 20\cos60° = 10\,\text{N}$. $F_y = 20\sin60° = 20\cdot(\sqrt{3}/2) = 10\sqrt{3} \approx 17.32\,\text{N}$.]

A force of 50 N acts at 30° to the vertical. Resolve it into horizontal and vertical components. [Solution: Vertical (along which 30° is measured): $F_y = 50\cos30° = 50\cdot(0.866) = 43.3\,\text{N}$. Horizontal: $F_x = 50\sin30° = 50\cdot0.5 = 25\,\text{N}$.]

Find the components of a 100 N force at 45° below the horizontal (third quadrant). [Solution: $F_x = 100\cos45° = 70.7\,\text{N}$ (positive, along +x). $F_y = -100\sin45° = -70.7\,\text{N}$ (negative, since below x-axis).]

A vector makes angles 60°, 45°, and 60° with the x, y, and z axes respectively. If its magnitude is 20, find its components. [Solution: $F_x = 20\cos60° = 10$, $F_y = 20\cos45° = 20/\sqrt{2} = 10\sqrt{2} \approx 14.14$, $F_z = 20\cos60° = 10$. Check: $100 + 200 + 100 = 400 = 20^2$ ✓]

A body of 5 kg is pushed with horizontal force 30 N. Find the normal reaction from the ground. [Solution: $W = mg = 5\cdot9.8 = 49\,\text{N}$ (down). $N = W = 49\,\text{N}$ (up). The horizontal force doesn't affect the vertical equilibrium since there is no vertical component.]

Resolve a force of 40 N at 53° above the horizontal into components, using $\sin53°=0.8$ and $\cos53°=0.6$. [Solution: $F_x = 40\cdot0.6 = 24\,\text{N}$, $F_y = 40\cdot0.8 = 32\,\text{N}$. This is a 3-4-5 right triangle scaled by 8.]

A force of 60 N is applied at 30° to the horizontal. Find (a) the horizontal component, (b) the vertical component, and (c) verify that $F^2 = F_x^2 + F_y^2$. [Solution: (a) $F_x = 60\cos30° = 60\cdot(0.866) = 51.96\,\text{N}$. (b) $F_y = 60\sin30° = 30\,\text{N}$. (c) $51.96^2 + 30^2 = 2700 + 900 = 3600 = 60^2$ ✓]

A 2 kg ball is thrown at 30° above the horizontal with speed 20 m/s. Find the initial horizontal and vertical velocity components. [Solution: $v_x = 20\cos30° = 20\cdot(0.866) = 17.32\,\text{m/s}$. $v_y = 20\sin30° = 10\,\text{m/s}$.]

A vector $\vec{A}$ has magnitude 10 and makes angles 60°, 60°, and 90° with the x, y, and z axes respectively. Find its components. [Solution: $A_x = 10\cos60° = 5$, $A_y = 10\cos60° = 5$, $A_z = 10\cos90° = 0$. Check: $25+25+0 = 50 \neq 100$. This is inconsistent — the given angles are impossible for a single vector. Valid angles must satisfy $\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1$.]

Find the components of the vector $\vec{r} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 12\hat{k}$ along the directions of the unit vectors $\hat{u}_1 = \frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\hat{u}_2 = \frac{\hat{j}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{2}}$. [Solution: Component along $\hat{u}_1$: $\vec{r}\cdot\hat{u}_1 = \frac{3+4+0}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{7}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 4.95$. Component along $\hat{u}_2$: $\vec{r}\cdot\hat{u}_2 = \frac{0+4+12}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{16}{\sqrt{2}} = 8\sqrt{2} \approx 11.31$.]

A force of 100 N makes angles of 60° with the x-axis and 45° with the y-axis. Find the angle with the z-axis and the z-component. [Solution: $\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1$. $\cos^260° + \cos^245° + \cos^2\gamma = 1$. $0.25 + 0.5 + \cos^2\gamma = 1$. $\cos^2\gamma = 0.25$, so $\gamma = 60°$ or $120°$. Taking $\gamma = 60°$: $F_z = 100\cos60° = 50\,\text{N}$. The components are $F_x = 50\,\text{N}$, $F_y = 70.7\,\text{N}$, $F_z = 50\,\text{N}$. Check: $2500+5000+2500 = 10000 = 100^2$ ✓]

State which of the following pairs of vectors are like, unlike, coplanar, or equal: (a) $\vec{A} = 3\hat{i}$, $\vec{B} = 7\hat{i}$. (b) $\vec{A} = 4\hat{j}$, $\vec{B} = -6\hat{j}$. (c) $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}$, $\vec{B} = 2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}$. [Solution: (a) like, coplanar, not equal (different magnitudes). (b) unlike, coplanar, not equal. (c) equal (and therefore like, coplanar, parallel).]
Find the unit vector along $\vec{A} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$. [Solution: $|\vec{A}| = \sqrt{9+16} = 5$. $\hat{A} = \vec{A}/|\vec{A}| = (3/5)\hat{i} + (4/5)\hat{j}$.]

Are the vectors $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$, $\vec{B} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{C} = 3\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$ coplanar? [Solution: Compute the scalar triple product $\vec{A}\cdot(\vec{B}\times\vec{C})$. First, $\vec{B}\times\vec{C} = \hat{i}((-2)(5)-(1)(1)) - \hat{j}((1)(5)-(1)(3)) + \hat{k}((1)(1)-(-2)(3)) = -11\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$. Then $\vec{A}\cdot(\vec{B}\times\vec{C}) = 2(-11) + 3(-2) + 4(7) = -22 - 6 + 28 = 0$. Since the scalar triple product is 0, the vectors are coplanar.]

Show that the zero vector $\vec{0}$ is parallel to every vector. [Solution: For any $\vec{A}$, the zero vector can be written as $\vec{0} = 0\cdot\vec{A}$. The scalar multiplier is 0, which is a non-negative real number. So $\vec{0}$ is parallel to $\vec{A}$ by the definition of parallelism. Also, $\vec{0}$ has no specific direction, so the convention treats it as parallel to all directions.]

If $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are unit vectors making 60° with each other, find $\vec{A}+\vec{B}$. [Solution: $|\vec{A}+\vec{B}| = \sqrt{1+1+2\cos60°} = \sqrt{2+1} = \sqrt{3}$. Direction: bisects the angle, so 30° from each. $\vec{A}+\vec{B} = \sqrt{3}\hat{n}$, where $\hat{n}$ is the unit vector at 30° from both.]

Determine whether the vectors $\vec{A} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{B} = \hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$, $\vec{C} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ are coplanar. [Solution: $\vec{B}\times\vec{C} = \hat{i}((-3)(3)-(5)(-1)) - \hat{j}((1)(3)-(5)(2)) + \hat{k}((1)(-1)-(-3)(2)) = -4\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$. $\vec{A}\cdot(\vec{B}\times\vec{C}) = 3(-4) + (-2)(7) + 1(5) = -12 - 14 + 5 = -21 \neq 0$. Not coplanar.]

Express the vector $\vec{F} = 6\hat{i} + 8\hat{j}$ in terms of its magnitude and a unit vector along it. [Solution: $|\vec{F}| = \sqrt{36+64} = 10$. $\hat{F} = (6/10)\hat{i} + (8/10)\hat{j} = 0.6\hat{i} + 0.8\hat{j}$. $\vec{F} = 10(0.6\hat{i}+0.8\hat{j}) = 10\hat{F}$.]

Given $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}$ and $\vec{B} = -4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j}$, show that the vectors are anti-parallel. [Solution: $\vec{B} = -2(2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}) = -2\vec{A}$. The negative scalar indicates opposite direction. So $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are anti-parallel. Verify: $B/A = |-4\hat{i}+6\hat{j}|/|2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}| = \sqrt{52}/\sqrt{13} = 2$. The ratio is negative, confirming anti-parallel.]

Find three unit vectors that are mutually perpendicular to each other. [Solution: The standard unit vectors $\hat{i}$, $\hat{j}$, $\hat{k}$ are mutually perpendicular: $\hat{i}\cdot\hat{j}=0$, $\hat{j}\cdot\hat{k}=0$, $\hat{k}\cdot\hat{i}=0$. Any rotation of this set also gives three mutually perpendicular unit vectors.]

Show that the vectors $\vec{A} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$, $\vec{B} = -\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, and $\vec{C} = \vec{B} - \vec{A} = -2\hat{i} + \hat{k}$ form a triangle. Find its type and area. [Solution: $\vec{A}+\vec{C} = \hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{i}+\hat{k} = -\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k} = \vec{B}$, so the triangle closes. Magnitudes: $|\vec{A}|=\sqrt{2}$, $|\vec{B}|=\sqrt{3}$, $|\vec{C}|=\sqrt{5}$. Check: $2+3=5$, so $|\vec{A}|^2+|\vec{B}|^2 = |\vec{C}|^2$ — it is a right-angled triangle with the right angle between $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$. Verify: $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = -1+1+0 = 0$. Area $= \frac{1}{2}|\vec{A}||\vec{B}| = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{2}\sqrt{3} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{2} \approx 1.225$.]

If $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are unit vectors with $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = 1/2$, find the angle between them and the magnitude of $\vec{A}+\vec{B}$. [Solution: $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = |\vec{A}||\vec{B}|\cos\theta = \cos\theta = 1/2$, so $\theta = 60°$. $|\vec{A}+\vec{B}| = \sqrt{1+1+2\cos60°} = \sqrt{2+1} = \sqrt{3}$.]

Three mutually perpendicular unit vectors $\hat{u}_1$, $\hat{u}_2$, $\hat{u}_3$ form a basis for 3D space. Express an arbitrary vector $\vec{A} = 5\hat{i} + 12\hat{j}$ in terms of this basis. [Solution: The standard basis $\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}$ IS a set of three mutually perpendicular unit vectors. $\vec{A}$ is already expressed in this basis: $A_x = 5$, $A_y = 12$, $A_z = 0$. The magnitude is $|\vec{A}| = \sqrt{25+144} = 13$.]

Find $\vec{A} \times \vec{B}$ where $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{B} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$. Using the determinant: $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(12 - 2) - \hat{j}(8 + 1) + \hat{k}(-4 - 3) = 10\hat{i} - 9\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}$.

Show that $\vec{A} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$ and $\vec{B} = 6\hat{i} + 8\hat{j}$ are parallel using the cross product. $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 6 & 8 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{k}(24 - 24) = 0$. Since the cross product is zero, the vectors are parallel. ✓

Find the unit vector perpendicular to both $\vec{A} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$ and $\vec{B} = \hat{j} + \hat{k}$. $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(1) - \hat{j}(1) + \hat{k}(1) = \hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$. Magnitude: $\sqrt{1 + 1 + 1} = \sqrt{3}$. Unit vector: $\hat{n} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k})$.

Calculate the torque $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$ where $\vec{r} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$ m and $\vec{F} = 4\hat{i} - 5\hat{j}$ N. $\vec{\tau} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 4 & -5 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{k}(-10 - 12) = -22\hat{k}$ N·m. The torque is 22 N·m clockwise (into the page).

Find the area of the triangle with vertices at $A(1,0,0)$, $B(0,2,0)$, and $C(0,0,3)$. Vectors: $\vec{AB} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}$, $\vec{AC} = -\hat{i} + 3\hat{k}$. $\vec{AB} \times \vec{AC} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ -1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(6) - \hat{j}(-3) + \hat{k}(2) = 6\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$. Area = $\frac{1}{2}|\vec{AB} \times \vec{AC}| = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{36 + 9 + 4} = \frac{\sqrt{49}}{2} = 3.5$ square units.

If $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = 6\hat{k}$ and $|\vec{A}| = 3$, $|\vec{B}| = 4$, find the angle between $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$. $|\vec{A} \times \vec{B}| = AB\sin\theta$. $6 = 3 \times 4 \times \sin\theta$. $\sin\theta = 6/12 = 0.5$. $\theta = 30°$ or $150°$. Since the result is $+6\hat{k}$, using the right-hand rule, the angle from $\vec{A}$ to $\vec{B}$ is 30° (counterclockwise looking down the +z axis).
